profiles.failureModes: The filament must be dried in the device with exact thermoregulation (ideally laboratory dryer) – before drying the whole spool, put a little piece of filament into the device for the test of functionality. If the material becomes softer or loses its original shape, lower the drying temperature. In the case of loss of transparency, use a different device. The spool can’t be put into the environment without a controlled value of relative humidity after drying. The cooling process must be taken in the desiccator (or in the sealing box with the content of silica gel). If the hot spool is placed into an environment with higher humidity, the moisture may be absorbed back in about 10 minutes. And possibly on a higher level of moisture than it was before drying! The coil should not be left in the dryer after it has been switched off, as there is still evaporated moisture in the environment which can be absorbed back into the filament in the same way. For Nylon materials, the drying temperature must not exceed 80 °C, otherwise, oxo-degradation of the polymer will occur.

coverage.finding: Reviewed 2026-09-30: Fillamentum Nylon AF80 Aramid (G154-01), Q05012, R-FILLAMENTUM-Technical-Data-Sheet-Nylon-AF80-Aramid, p. 1. Maker names parts under constant stress, including bearings, cogwheels and reinforcement parts; no component load, fatigue life or finished-part qualification follows. Claims remain in maker know-how and cannot pass selection. Other products remain individually bounded.
Canonical identity recorded: Polyamide 12 (Nylon 12) (Aramid fibre) (Nylon / Polyamide, base polymer PA12). Aliases and disputed entries are family entries of their own.
H2C status "Theoretical" is recorded with no document cited behind it.
7 mechanical measurement(s) of this material's own grades. See specimen, direction, moisture, preparation and standard before comparing.
Its own products publish no thermal value.
3 print profile(s) publishing a nozzle, bed, chamber or drying setting: P1026, P1380, P1394. Check other setup fields individually.
No exposure, solubility or moisture record from its own sources. Its base polymer's published behaviour is shown instead, labelled polymer-level.

Not published by its own products: Compression strength, Coefficient of thermal expansion, Thermal conductivity, Fracture toughness, Fatigue life, Creep compliance, Coefficient of friction.

knowHow.text: The material can be with the advantage used for printing parts that are under constant stress, for example, bearings, cogwheels, reinforcement parts etc.
The reinforcement brings tribological properties and wear resistance to the material.
It can withstand higher static pressure load than unfilled Nylon FX256.
These great properties are preserved even at low temperatures.
The printing properties, processing stability and rheology are improved thanks to the content of aramid fibres.

polymerEnvironment.finding: Irreversible chemical damage to the material can only be caused by water or aqueous solutions at high temperatures. This is referred to as hydrolysis... polyamide 12 is considerably more resistant to hydrolysis than polyamide 6 and polyamide 66.
Good to very good resistance to greases, oils, fuels, hydraulic fluids, and many solvents as well as to salt solutions, etc.
polymerEnvironment.notes: The brochure's chemical resistance table (p. 21-22) is colour-coded and could not be transcribed from the PDF text; only the text statements are recorded.

polymerEnvironment.finding: In general, it can be said that long-chain, semi-crystalline polyamides absorb little water, are resistant to polar and non-polar solvents, exhibit low creep behavior and high impact resistance... Good to very good resistance to greases, oils, fuels, hydraulic fluids, and many solvents.
polymerEnvironment.notes: Class-level statement; the rated table (p. 21-22) is colour-coded and could not be transcribed.

polymerEnvironment.agent: Hot water or moist air at higher temperatures
polymerEnvironment.finding: Polycondensation products, to which polyamides also belong, have a limited resistance to hot water or moist air at higher temperatures. PA 12 has good hydrolysis resistance compared to other polyamides, but it is gradually molecularly degraded by hot water. Compounds with a high molecular mass will last longer than those with a low molecular mass. Hydrolytic degradation occurs faster in acid media than in neutral or alkaline media. Standard compounds are resistant to pure water to about 70 or 80 °C.

Exposure to short wave light of wavelengths less than 400 nm results in an accelerated decrease in the molecular mass of the polymers, causing molded parts and semi-finished products to become brittle. Light stabilizers, UV absorbers and/or radical scavengers considerably reduce weathering damage. However, the best protection is provided by suitable grades of carbon black, if blackening is possible.
Most VESTAMID compounds are flammable. At mass temperatures above 350 °C flammable gases form through decomposition.
polymerEnvironment.notes: No UL 94 rating for the neat resin is stated. Verdict convention used in this table: burns / UL 94 HB = not-resistant, V-1 or V-2 = limited, V-0 = resistant.
